entries.title: The average fill / exit lines stop jumping around.
entries.text: The line was being re-placed on most price updates even though your average hadn't changed. It now moves only when a buy or sell changes the average. Checked live on Axiom: over 75 s, with the coin moving between $37K and $47K, the line held one level.

entries.title: "Avg entry MC" and the chart's avg-fill line now agree.
entries.text: Two causes. The supply PaperTrench worked from drifted (seen live: 1.09B on a 1B-supply coin, so an entry read $41.0K instead of $37.6K); it now uses the coin's real supply when it's known. And a fill's market cap was recorded before slippage while its price was recorded after, so with a high slippage setting the panel and the line sat exactly that far apart ($69.9K vs $58.2K at 20%). A fill now carries one price in every unit. If you run a high slippage setting, your fill markers and avg line now sit at the price you actually got, off the candle by that slippage.

entries.title: A sell can no longer be booked at a lagging price the chain disagrees with.
entries.text: "Bought at 17k, sold at 40k, shows sold at 17k": when the screen had been quiet for a few seconds, an outside quote that agreed with the old price could price the sell even though the chain read said otherwise. That sell is now refused with the reason shown, and outside quotes are held to a tighter agreement before they may fill. Proven in tests, not reproduced live; it means a refusal where there used to be a wrong fill.

entries.title: Profit no longer shows on a rugged coin.
entries.text: A price from a collapsed pool was already kept out of the position's mark, but the panel still displayed it and a take-profit could fire on it. It is now refused before the panel takes it. TP / SL / trailing orders also wait for a price that is actually fresh. This covers the dead-pool price; a position whose price feed simply stops still shows its last mark.

entries.title: Missing buys and positions: six causes fixed.
entries.text: (1) A buy whose save got no answer from the background worker wrote the whole wallet over anything another window had just saved; it now checks first and merges. (2) A window that had fallen behind could later overwrite newer trades. (3) A coin opened by its new pool after migrating did not find the position filed under the old bonding-curve address, including when the pool list wasn't published yet or the coin was only on Jupiter. (4) A chain lookup that got no answer was never tried again until reload. (5) Sells made before a position was moved to its real address were left out of SOLD and "sell initial". (6) Found while testing live with the background worker deliberately held: a buy said "Bought" and was then erased, because a routine save that gave up could undo the buy's save counter and let a stale queued save overwrite it. After the fix, five buys in a row under the same conditions all stayed. All proven in tests; we have not reproduced each report live, so if a buy still goes missing, hit Share debug logs right then.

entries.title: "Fetching live price…" on a brand-new coin no longer gets stuck after three failed chain reads.
entries.text: The read is retried every 30 s instead of never. On Axiom's new coin pages this state was already rare; this covers launches the price sites haven't listed yet.

entries.title: A quick-buy right after opening a new pair can't arm for the coin you just left.
Chip buys on Axiom use Axiom's own price on more rows.
entries.text: Rows quoted in something other than SOL are now read from Axiom's feed too, but only when that price agrees with the row you tapped; on its own that feed is right for some coins and far off for others.

entries.title: X-Ray: follower counts load on X's newer profile layout,
entries.text: a first visit starts the follower read instead of waiting for a second visit (with deep scan on, that can be one extra request to X per newly visited profile, inside the existing budget), and the card says plainly when follower lists or posts haven't been read instead of showing "Reading follower lists…" forever or a green "None found". Checked on a live X profile (@onlyterp): the card showed 58.9K followers and 5.1K following, matching X's own header.

entries.title: Lag and freezes with a big wallet or many open positions.
entries.text: Three causes measured and fixed: the whole wallet (about 1 MB for a full journal) was re-read and re-saved every 0.8 s whether or not anything changed, and every other open tab decoded it again; every price tick rebuilt a number formatter hundreds of times for the positions bar; and the scan that finds list rows could spend a long time walking one row's data. Measured in a real browser with a full wallet (2,000 fills, 150 open positions): on the Pulse list the released 3.28.0 kept the page's main thread busy for 17 of 61 seconds; this build, 0.2 seconds. On a coin's page it was 2.1 seconds against 0.04, and wallet saves went from 54 a minute to none while nothing changed.

entries.title: A chip buy no longer books a lagging outside price when the row said otherwise.
entries.text: When Axiom's feed doesn't cover a row, the buy was priced by an outside quote that could trail the row badly (seen live: an $82.5K row booked $61.8K while the coin's own page confirmed about $81K). If that quote is more than 5% from the cap the row showed when you tapped (and within the 2x sanity limit, beyond which the buy is refused), the buy is now booked at the row's cap. Only for coins on the standard 1B supply, where the two caps are counted the same way.

entries.title: Coins the price sites don't cover can be chip-bought on Axiom.
entries.text: Some new coins are quoted in tokens the outside price sites don't convert, so nothing priced them and the tap waited and expired. The buy is now priced from the market cap the row shows and the supply Axiom reports for it. The rule is the size of the buy: up to 2% of the coin's market cap fills at the row's price. A bigger share has no honest price (0.1 SOL into a $1 coin is several times its whole supply), so that tap is refused at once with the reason. A chip buy that does have to wait for a price now says so immediately instead of sitting silent for up to 60 s.

entries.title: Stale positions are flagged, and a reopened coin that really moved can be sold.
entries.text: Every mark now carries its time: a position nobody has re-priced for two minutes is shown faded on the positions bar instead of looking live, and a sell against such an old mark is no longer refused just because the price moved (anything more than 2x from the mark still needs a second source).

entries.title: Brand-new pump coins above a $100K market cap are priced before the price sites list them,
Smaller fixes.
entries.text: While a page switches from the bonding curve to the new pool, the card says "Confirming coin…" instead of showing a coin you hold as empty. A SOL/USD rate worked out from a non-Solana coin's price is only used when it matches the known SOL rate. The replay tape and the copied fill line show the same P&L as the journal row (they showed a figure that left the buy fee out). Axiom links from the positions bar and dashboard go straight to the new coin page instead of through a redirect. The update banner and README now say to press Reload and never Remove: removing the extension deletes your wallet.

entries.title: Checked and found already fixed:
entries.text: sell amounts when clipping (3.24.0), wallet reset on update (the permanent extension ID from 3.26.0; the remaining way to lose a wallet is clicking Remove), profit on a rug after selling (3.10/3.12), quick-buy chip covering the market cap, Robinhood / BNB routing, the onboarding step that never ticked.

entries.title: Checked against the "showed $50, received $20" report:
entries.text: since 3.24.0 the panel's "If you sell now" line is computed by the same code that books the sell, fees and slippage included; a test now pins that the two are equal.

entries.title: Settings open even when the browser refuses the settings page (the Opera report).
entries.text: If the browser won't open it the normal way, the dashboard opens as a regular tab instead. Not tested in Opera itself.

entries.title: What is left:
entries.text: the settings fallback could not be tried in Opera itself (it is not installed on our test machine). The freeze fixes were measured in tests, not in a real browser trace, so if you still get lag, a performance recording will tell us where.
